text:
maya: Quick heads-up — onboarding spectra-1.2 embeddings shows odd k‑means fragmentation on a small wiki slice, posting numbers and plots. Anyone free to triage?

jon: can you drop the metrics and config? link to the UMAP images would help (or s3).

maya: summary below, pasted from eval run on stg3:
```
Model: spectra-1.2
Dataset: wiki-short-2k (mix of short/long queries)
Mode: FP16 vs INT4 (per-channel)
FP16 recall@10: 0.82
INT4 recall@10: 0.78   (-4 pts)
cosine avg intra-cluster sim: 0.67 -> 0.54 (drop)
short queries (len<8) recall@10: 0.64 -> 0.49
index params: hnsw M=32, ef_construction=200, ef_search=64
```

lina: is the search using cosine or dot? also, pooling/normalization config? small queries are usually sensitive to post-norm.

sam: FYI: int4 per-channel can flip signs near zero — that will fragment clusters if embeddings aren't well centered.

maya: current config snippet we used:
```
embed_config:
  pooling: mean
  normalize: false
  quant: int4-perchannel
  post_norm: false
```

lina: try set post_norm: true and re-run cosine search. that often recovers short-query recall by removing scale variance. also compare with dot product on non-normalized vectors.

maya: did a quick A/B: post_norm true improved short-query recall from 0.49 -> 0.52 and overall recall@10 +0.03, but clusters still show fragmentation in UMAP (attached images to s3: s3://redwood-qa/spectra/umap_frag_v1.png).

infra-bot: deploy finished: staging/spectra-1.2-int4 at stg3 (build 2026-03-20T09:12Z) :white_check_mark:

jon: can you dump a handful of failure cases (embeddings + nearest neighbors) so we can inspect sign patterns? command I use:
```
python -m rinfra.eval.dump_embeddings --model spectra-1.2 --mode int4 --ids 512 --out /tmp/spectra_dump.npz
```

maya: dump uploaded to s3://redwood-qa/spectra/dumps/spectra_dump_2524680000.npz and a tiny repro script at gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/spectra-mini-repro (includes how to load wandb/npz).

lina: next experiments to isolate: 1) FP16 vs INT4 on same seed (sanity), 2) per-sample normalization before indexing, 3) try ef_search 128 and see recall change, 4) run cosine vs dot.

sam: also suggested: run calibration with clipped-quant (tiny floor) to avoid sign flips near zero, and check embedding variance per-dim (maybe one dim dominates).

jon: if you can reproduce locally on 512 examples we'll iterate faster — otherwise we can schedule a larger job on dedicated infra.

maya: starting local 512 run with FP16 / INT4 / post_norm true / ef_search 128, will post numbers in ~40m. ping me if you want access to the session.

jon: cool — if you see per-dim stdev >> others, try PCA-whitening as a quick experiment to reduce dominance.

maya: noted. thanks all — will update soon. :coffee:
